concepts.notes: Permanently installed roof machine (track- or parapet-mounted roof car, or monorail-based) that lowers a cradle down the façade for cleaning and maintenance. US regulations call it a "powered platform" (OSHA 1910.66, ASME A120.1); UK/EU codes treat it as permanently installed suspended access equipment (BS 6037-1, EN 1808). GCC tenders usually bundle it under Division 11 24 23 with monorails, davits and anchors, and buyers there often say "cradle machine" or "gondola". Russian has no single normative term; "BMU" is used as-is.

The self-propelled carriage of a BMU that travels on roof rails or a paved runway and carries the jib/arm and cradle. In Gulf Arabic "ونش" (winch/crane) is used loosely, so "ونش سطح" may mean the whole roof machine.

Arm on a BMU roof car that reaches over the parapet or setbacks; luffing changes the arm angle, telescoping changes its length, slewing rotates it. Specs quote reach (outreach) and working load of the cradle.

The suspended work platform itself. Cradles that belong to a BMU, monorail or davit installation are Division 11 scope (route to bmu/wce when those words appear); stand-alone, rented or replacement platforms are cradle work (see temporary_suspended_platform). GCC buyers say "cradle" for both, so check whether the enquiry is a permanent installation, a replacement cradle, or a monthly rental.

Fixed rail (roof edge, parapet or soffit) from which a cradle, bosun chair or rope-access trolley travels with an electric or manual hoist. Used where a BMU is uneconomic or cannot reach (atria, setbacks, curved façades).

Fixed or portable arms set into roof sockets/bases to suspend a cradle or rope at defined drops; a lower-cost alternative to a BMU or monorail. The Russian "консоль" also covers counterweighted outrigger beams of temporary platforms.

Certified anchorages and lifelines for rope access and as secondary protection on cradles (EN 795 / BS 7883 in UK-EU, ANSI/ASSP Z359 and ANSI/IWCA I-14.1 in the US). Usually a separate BOQ line under the façade-access section; periodic recertification is a recurring service.

Technicians working on twin ropes from certified anchors (IRATA / SPRAT schemes). Enquiries can be for the anchor/davit equipment (this category) or for cleaning/repair labour (route those to other_work). In Russia the trade is called "промышленный альпинизм".

Tender umbrella for the permanent equipment that lets a building be cleaned (BMU, monorail, davits, anchors, travelling ladders). Some buyers use it loosely for a spider platform or even for a cleaning service — read the BOQ before classifying.

Umbrella for BMU, monorail, davit, anchor, gantry and travelling-ladder systems (MasterFormat 11 24 23 "Façade Access Equipment"; BS 6037 "permanently installed access equipment"). Classify by the specific system when the enquiry names one; BMU-led packages belong to bmu.

A labour/service contract (often monthly or per cycle) rather than equipment supply; frequently requested by facility-management companies together with maintenance of the building's cleaning machines.
Cleaning of glazing (curtain walls, skylights, windows). "Window cleaning" alone is ambiguous: with "system/equipment/unit" it means equipment (wce/bmu), otherwise a service.

Motorised platform (typically ZLP630/ZLP800 class, 2–12 m long) hung from counterweighted roof outriggers or parapet clamps, with traction hoists, safety locks and wire ropes. Sold or rented monthly; installation and "shifting" between drops are priced separately. UK code: BS 5974; EU: EN 1808; US: OSHA 1926.451/.452.
Spare-part vocabulary that signals a cradle repair/parts enquiry rather than a new system; Gulf Arabic quotations commonly transliterate English part names.
Rack-and-pinion mast(s) with a wide work deck that climbs the façade; standard EN 1495. Supplied by the same fleets as construction hoists, so it is filed under hoist.

Temporary site lift on a tied mast (single/twin cage) for workers and/or materials; standards EN 12159 / EN 12158, OSHA 1926.552, ANSI A10.4. Rental quotes normally cover mast height, ties, erection/climbing, operator and monthly rate.
Hoist certified to carry people. Caution: in Gulf Arabic "رافعة أفراد" usually means a man lift (MEWP), not a personnel hoist.

Self-propelled or truck-mounted boom platforms. Size is quoted as working height (about platform height + 2 m). In US OSHA text "manlift" can also mean a belt manlift inside buildings; on construction sites it means a boom lift. Rental enquiries often add operator, transport and third-party inspection certificates.
Narrow tracked boom on outriggers for atria, malls, hospitals and soft ground; sometimes specified as the "window cleaning system" for low/medium buildings.
Vertical-only MEWP (electric slab or diesel rough-terrain). Enquiries state working height (e.g., 10–22 m), drive type and rental period (day/week/month).
Rental quotes list jib length, height under hook, capacity at tip, mobilisation/demobilisation, erection/climbing, operator and monthly rate; standards EN 14439, ASME B30.3.
Gulf "ونش" alone can also mean a tow truck (ونش سحب) or a winch, so require a crane/lifting context before classifying.
Note that Gulf Arabic "سقالة" is also used for suspended platforms ("سقالة معلقة/كهربائية") — check for motor/wire-rope words before routing to scaffolding instead of cradle.

Standards (verticals) with cup joints taking ledgers (horizontals); Gulf Arabic quotations use قائم for standard, عارضة/ليدجر for ledger and جاك قاعدة for base jack. Very common in GCC and India for façade and falsework support.
Rosette/wedge-connection systems. In Russian practice "клиновые" (wedge) and "хомутовые" (clamp) are the usual family names.
Loose 48.3 mm tubes joined by couplers (EN 39 / EN 74; UK guidance NASC TG20).
Prefabricated welded frames with cross braces; often rented by lot/area.
Castor-mounted towers (EN 1004; PASMA training in the UK).
Node-and-member steel grids for long-span roofs, domes, canopies (petrol stations, entrances) and skylight substructures; usually design-fabricate-install packages priced per m² or lump sum.
Often needs its own cleaning access (gantry, travelling ladder) — a frequent cross-sell into wce.
Steel-frame with PVC/PVDF membrane or metal sheet; filed with space frames as light steel roof structures.

Scope: scheduled preventive visits (often monthly), lubrication, functional and load tests, call-outs. "Comprehensive" (India: CMC) includes spare parts; "labour-only" / "without spare parts" excludes them — always capture which.
Handover deliverable (manuals, as-built drawings, test certificates, training) and also the name of operate-and-maintain contracts.
US projects rarely issue BOQs (bidders price drawings/specs on bid forms). Russian "смета" is a priced estimate rather than an unpriced BOQ.
GCC main contractors send "pre-tender" RFQs to specialists before submitting their own bid; the closing date and tender number are the key fields to extract.
Our outgoing document; a supplier's quotation to us is a vendor_offer, not a work enquiry.
Signals a won job: link to the quotation reference and start the project.
Public tenders reach specialists through main contractors; mails carry tender numbers, closing dates, site-visit dates and addenda.
Changes BOQ/specs or the closing date; must be attached to the existing project, not opened as a new enquiry. In Arabic, "ملحق" also names a contract extension (e.g., maintenance addendum).
Questions raised before the tender query deadline; answers usually come back as an addendum.
Post-award approval package (data sheets, calculations, shop drawings, method statement) sent to the consultant via the main contractor.
Installation/erection sequence with risk assessment; in Russia the closest equivalent is the "проект производства работ (ППР)".

UK LOLER "thorough examination" (6-monthly for equipment lifting people); GCC clients ask for third-party inspection certificates (TPI) for each machine and sometimes for operators; Russia: technical examination under the lifting-structures rules.

CSI MasterFormat: 11 24 00 Maintenance Equipment → 11 24 23 Façade Access Equipment (BMU, davits, monorails, anchors). GCC consultants reuse CSI numbering in specifications and BOQs, so "Div-11" in a subject line is a strong bmu/wce signal.
Rates are quoted per day/week/month with minimum period, transport (mobilisation/demobilisation) and operator as separate lines.
